name: International Business Machines Corporation
executive_summary: International Business Machines Corporation (IBM) screens as a **Strong Buy** on quantitative value metrics—FCF yield (~5.9%), dividend yield (~3.3%), quality and earnings-quality factors—despite reported revenue growth of roughly −1.8%. The investment case rests on a software-led hybrid cloud and AI platform (HashiCorp, Confluent), recurring revenue, and durable cash generation that has historically funded a progressive dividend. At ~18.4× P/E and ~6.1× P/B, the market prices a cyclical infrastructure downturn and AI-disruption risk more than the screen’s cash-return profile. The central debate is whether the July 2026 earnings shock—revenue guidance cut, mainframe weakness, and a historic share-price fall—marks a temporary cycle trough or a structural reset of enterprise IT spending priorities.
investment_thesis:
The quantitative screen passes nine of 22 models across five factor families (cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, risk), with a composite score of 74% and high data completeness (20/20 metrics). That profile fits a value investor seeking income plus FCF-backed quality rather than pure growth: FCF Yield, Neff PEGY (0.06), Buffett Quality, High Dividend Yield, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Composite Value, Earnings Quality and Quality Value all pass. ROE of 34.5% reflects improved profitability after the 2024 earnings trough, though it is flattered by a goodwill-heavy balance sheet and negative tangible book.

Business quality, as disclosed in SEC filings, is anchored in three segments—Software, Consulting and Infrastructure—with Software the strategic engine. In Q2 2026 (10-Q, filed 23 July 2026), Software revenue rose 5.1% year-on-year to $7.8bn; Hybrid Cloud and Automation grew, while Transaction Processing declined. Consulting was flat (+0.2%); Infrastructure fell 7.4%, consistent with post-z17 mainframe cycle dynamics referenced in the filing. Remaining performance obligations stood at approximately **$68bn** at 30 June 2026, with ~69% expected within two years—a substantial backlog supporting revenue visibility.

M&A reinforces the AI/data platform thesis: HashiCorp closed February 2025 (per FY2025 10-K); Confluent closed 17 March 2026 for ~$11.6bn (Q2 2026 10-Q). The screen’s cheapness signal likely reflects market scepticism after the July 2026 selloff rather than deteriorating cash economics: H1 2026 operating cash flow was **$7.8bn** against capital/software investment of ~$0.8bn, implying annualised FCF well above the dividend outlay (~$6.3bn annualised from H1 dividends of $3.2bn).

INVESTUAL REVIEW

**Data source note:** Annual 10-K body extracts (FY2024 filed February 2025; FY2025 filed February 2026) incorporate financial statements by reference to the Annual Report and do **not** contain line-item figures in the available text extracts. Annual trends below therefore fall back to **`financials_annual.json` (Yahoo)**. Interim figures are taken from 10-Q body extracts where available.

**Annual trends (Yahoo fallback)**

| Metric | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | $61.9bn | $62.8bn | $67.5bn |
| Operating income | $9.4bn | $10.1bn | $12.5bn |
| Net income | $7.5bn | $6.0bn | $10.6bn |
| Diluted EPS | $8.14 | $6.43 | $11.17 |
| Free cash flow | $12.1bn | $11.8bn | $11.5bn |

Revenue grew ~9% in FY2025, with net income and EPS rebounding sharply from FY2024, when results were depressed by non-operating items (including a pension settlement charge visible in the Q3 2025 10-Q comparative footnotes). FCF has been stable at $11–12bn across 2023–25, supporting the screen’s FCF Yield pass. FY2025 balance sheet (Yahoo): total assets **$151.9bn**, total debt **$64.6bn**, net debt **$47.7bn**, stockholders’ equity **$32.6bn**, goodwill plus intangibles **$79.1bn**—acquisition activity has materially increased intangible assets and leverage.

**Interim trends (primary 10-Q filings)**

*Q1 2026 (10-Q, 23 April 2026):* Revenue **$15.9bn** (+9.5% vs Q1 2025 $14.5bn); net income **$1.2bn** vs $1.1bn; diluted EPS **$1.28** vs $1.13.

*H1 2026 (10-Q, 23 July 2026):* Revenue **$33.1bn** (+4.9% vs H1 2025 $31.5bn); net income **$3.4bn** (+4.1%); diluted EPS **$3.55** vs $3.43. Operating cash flow **$7.8bn** (vs $6.1bn H1 2025). Cash fell from **$13.6bn** to **$7.2bn**, reflecting the Confluent acquisition (~$10.5bn net cash used for acquisitions in H1). Total debt rose to **~$62.0bn**; retirement and post-retirement obligations **$8.6bn**.

*Q2 2026 (same filing):* Revenue **$17.2bn** (+1.1% vs Q2 2025); net income **$2.2bn** (−1.3%); diluted EPS **$2.27** vs $2.31. Segment revenue: Software **$7.8bn** (+5.1%), Consulting **$5.3bn** (+0.2%), Infrastructure **$3.8bn** (−7.4%). Segment profit margins: Software 32.2%, Consulting 12.1%, Infrastructure 21.8%.

*Q2 2025 (10-Q, 24 July 2025):* Revenue **$17.0bn** (+7.7% vs Q2 2024); H1 2025 revenue **$31.5bn** (+4.3%).

*Q3 2025 (10-Q, 23 October 2025):* Nine-month revenue **$47.8bn** (+5.9% vs 9M 2024); nine-month net income **$5.0bn** vs $3.1bn (2024 comparatives distorted by pension settlement).

**Gaps:** 10-Q MD&A sections are truncated in the available body extracts (80,000-character limit), so full-year guidance language from the Q2 2026 earnings release is not verifiable from filing bodies. Eight 8-K filings in the index have no downloadable body text.
risks_and_flags:
**Infrastructure and cycle risk.** Q2 2026 Infrastructure revenue fell 7.4%; filings reference the z17 mainframe launch (June 2025) affecting lease residual accounting. News coverage (WSJ, 22 July 2026) cited data-centre mainframe sales down ~42%, aligning with cyclical exposure not fully captured by static value screens.

**AI strategy and competitive risk.** The FY2025 10-K flags that failure to maintain AI leadership, or unexpected AI outcomes, could harm reputation, margins and competitiveness. Management publicly defended the AI strategy after the July 2026 selloff (CNBC/Yahoo Finance, 23 July 2026), but enterprise deal delays and budget reallocation were cited as drivers of the warning.

**Leverage and M&A integration.** Confluent ($11.6bn) and HashiCorp add ~$8bn+ of goodwill/intangibles. H1 2026 investing cash outflows of **$11.0bn** and higher amortisation ($1.5bn H1) increase execution risk. Total debt ~$62bn; covenants require a consolidated net interest expense ratio of at least 2.20×—IBM reports compliance (Q2 2026 10-Q, note 12)—but rising rates and acquisition debt raise refinancing risk.

**Pension and retirement obligations.** FY2025 10-K warns that adverse financial markets could increase pension liabilities and require incremental funding, creating liquidity pressure. Prepaid pension assets of **$7.6bn** and retirement obligations of **$8.6bn** (30 June 2026 balance sheet) remain material, though no going-concern language appears in available filing extracts.

**Governance and legal.** FY2025 10-K references ongoing claims, tax matters and IP litigation (note Q incorporated by reference). A securities-fraud investigation notice was published following the July 2026 stock drop (PR Newswire, 21 July 2026). Contingency provisions recorded in Q2 2026 were not material (10-Q, note 14), but outcomes are inherently uncertain.

**Balance sheet quality.** Tangible book value is deeply negative (~−$46bn per Yahoo FY2025) due to goodwill from Red Hat, HashiCorp, Confluent and other deals—relevant for P/B interpretation. Share repurchases remain suspended (since 2019 Red Hat closing); capital return is dividend-led (~$6.3bn FY2025).
news_highlights:
**Coverage is thin:** the news manifest contains **53 articles, all dated July 2026**—effectively one week centred on Q2 earnings. No headlines span the prior eleven months; earlier strategic context must come from filings.

Material items from the manifest:

- **22 July 2026:** IBM releases Q2 results and lowers full-year revenue forecast after a preliminary warning cratered the stock (CNBC: *"IBM lowers full-year forecast after earnings warning"*; PR Newswire: *"IBM RELEASES SECOND-QUARTER RESULTS"*). Barron's (*23 July 2026*) noted a revenue miss but **maintained free cash flow outlook**.
- **22–23 July 2026:** WSJ (*"IBM Lowers Its Growth Outlook as Sales of Data-Center Mainframes Sink 42%"*); Yahoo Finance on CEO Arvind Krishna blaming an unanticipated client spending shift; TechCrunch on AI-not-killing-mainframe narrative.
- **21 July 2026:** PR Newswire securities-fraud investigation notice following ~25% stock drop.
- **24 July 2026:** Bernstein cut price target on deal delays and budget pressures (Investing.com); Seeking Alpha framed the rout as a *"Generational Opportunity."*
- **24 July 2026:** IBM joined Nvidia, Microsoft and Meta in an open-source AI letter to lawmakers (Yahoo Finance).
- **Ongoing:** Jim Cramer continued to defend the software/quantum thesis despite a ~26% share decline (*Yahoo Finance, 25 July 2026*).

M&A activity in filings (Confluent March 2026; pending Infrastructure-segment acquisition signed 22 July 2026) is not yet reflected in most news headlines.
research_rationale: Filing-backed FCF, dividend capacity and software backlog support the screen’s Strong Buy value case, but the July 2026 guidance cut, infrastructure cycle weakness and thin news history introduce near-term uncertainty that warrants accumulation rather than unqualified conviction.
